title: Volunteer as a tutor
intro: You do not need an account. A volunteer is verified on exactly the same basis as a paid tutor.
weeklyHours: Hours a week you can give
weeklyHoursHint: Be realistic. A volunteer who is over-committed stops turning up, and the family that loses those sessions is the one that could not pay for them.
motivation: Why do you want to volunteer?
motivationHint: In your own words, in any language. Stored exactly as you write it.

document.label: Attach a CV, degree or transcript
document.hint: PDF only, up to 5 MB, one file.
document.optionalNow: Optional now — you can send it later. It is required before an application can be approved, because verification is against documents.
document.private: It goes to a private store that only Ustaad.com administrators can open, through a link that expires. It is never public and never in the repository.
document.wrongType: Only a PDF can be attached. Nothing has been uploaded.
document.tooLarge: That file is larger than 5 MB. Nothing has been uploaded.

received: Your application has been recorded and the team has been notified. Verification is the same process a paid tutor goes through.

why.heading: Why this programme exists
why.reach: Some families cannot pay at any rate. A tuition market that only sells to those who can leaves those students with nothing, and no amount of matching fixes that.
why.supply: And the thinnest part of supply is the part that matters most: verified female tutors who will teach at a family’s home. Where a daughter is not permitted to travel to a centre, that tutor is the only route to any tuition at all.
why.standard: A volunteer is verified on exactly the same basis as a paid tutor — CNIC and academic documents, checked by an administrator. The fee is what differs, not the standard.

form.heading: Your application
form.noAccount: No account needed. Nothing here signs you up for anything.

success.heading: Your application has been received
success.saved: It is saved and in the queue. That record is what the team works from, and it exists now whatever happens to any email.
success.mailSent: An email is on its way to the team, and an acknowledgement to you.
success.mailFailed: The notification email did not go out — that is our problem, not yours, and it changes nothing about your application. The record is saved and the team will see it.
success.next: What happens next: an administrator reads it, and you will hear back within about a week. Before approval you will be asked for a CNIC and academic documents, exactly as any paid tutor is.
